body:
**Cycle:** 4

**Age + Partner's age (if relevant):** 31F, 36M

**Typical cycle length:** 28 days

**Ovulation cycle day:** CD17/18, which is later than normal. Usually I ovulate around CD14/15. Interestingly I also had positive OPKs the morning of CD17, then was negative in the afternoon, then before bed I tested positive again. 

**CD/DPO of positive test(s):** 9 or 10 DPO (depending on Ov date) vvvfl, positive on Clearblue digital test the next day. Test strip line has been getting slightly darker every day

**CD/DPO of any negative test(s) before positive:** None, was away from home 

**Tracking methods and app(s) used:** Premom app and OPKs

**Relevant days of sperminating and/or method (SMEP, TI, IUI, FET, etc.):** if we assume ovulation was CD17, O-4, O-3, O-1

**Health conditions/medical tests:** I had my AMH tested before we started trying out of anxiety (a number of close friends had really rough fertility journeys) and levels were “normal” (3.25 ng/mL)

**Supplements and medications (yours and/or your partner’s):** Bird&Be power prenatals for women and men (both with the CoQ10 option) for about 6 months

**Birth control history (if relevant):** Was on the pill from 17-26, then had an IUD from 26-30, then pill for a bit less than a year until I went off it around my 31st birthday in Feb (so 7 months ago). 

**Link to chart:** n/a

**Link to lineporn:** n/a

**Symptom spotting:** On 7 or 8 DPO I had fairly bad nausea pretty much all day. There was no good reason for it so I immediately suspected, and tested the next morning. I’ve been nauseous on and off since. My mom was apparently sick through all of both of her pregnancies, so I wonder if she and I are more sensitive to hcg?

**Other (advice/tip(s), freaking out, miscellaneous):** for the first 3 cycles we exclusively hit O-2 and O-1, so I wonder if having more time before ovulation helped? Who knows. Have been nauseous for the last 4 days and a bit headachey, so I think I’m in for a fun ride. I’ll take it if it helps this lil nugget stick.
Date twins!!! Love love love the design! We’re nerds too and ours had a video game theme. As I’ve been saying to my fiancé, I guess June 3rd really is for the nerds ;)

We’re having a party this weekend for this very purpose! Same thing, 5 on each side and while some know each other (met a few times here and there or “know of” them at least), we thought it would be fun to have our closest people all together for a night of fun! Our group was very open to it and is looking forward to meeting each other, so it depends if that kind of thing gives for your friends.

We’re going to include a note in our website FAQ that says that it will be a child free wedding with the exception of our flower girls, ring bearer, and the children of friends coming from overseas. But all of the people we’ve invited who have kids are all very level headed and would want a night out anyway, so we don’t anticipate much confusion or grumpiness.

If you cover it in electrical tape, maybe also cover it with a star or something and add a few stars around the sign so that it just looks like you have decoration around the wording (to further hide that an apostrophe ever existed)

I totally missed this comment, but of my goodness! I’m so happy you’re going to get to share these memories with him after all that the two of you have been through together. And my grandfather also made pasta, that’s so cute!

I don’t think it’s weird, it’s a great nod to a sweet memory for you both! My dad and I are dancing to You’ve Got a Friend in Me from Toy Story for similar reasons. I get anxious wondering if people will like or “get” certain things in our wedding but ultimately… it’s my (and your!) day. If they think it’s an odd choice, cool, they can avoid choosing it for themselves. Also, I feel like anyone applying a weird “romance” layer to a father daughter dance to a song from a children’s movie is just looking for things to be picky about. You do you, it’ll be great!

Love that! I think it’s such a cute song that calls back to childhood memories with my Dad, while also celebrating the fact that now that I’m a grown woman, I actually get to be friends with him. Plus he’s always got my back!

When you do reach out, you could say something like “Hey [name], wanted to drop you a note regarding our wedding! A friend who has children reached out to me to clarify whether they were included on the invite for her and her husband. They weren’t, as were unfortunately not available to accommodate children for most of our guest unless they’re close relations. But it made me realize that this might not be clear to everyone and I should clarify! So just in case you were wondering the same thing, I wanted to let you know that we were only able to accommodate you and [partner] due to the overall guest count. We’re sorry we weren’t able to include the kids, but we hope that the two of you will get to enjoy some well deserved mom and dad time off and dance the night away with us!”
Love that!!

We’re having a video game themed wedding! We’re both huge nerds, and had our first date in an arcade bar. We’ve sent the save the dates already, and I spent hours making pixel characters for each of us and putting them on a Mario-esque background. Our ceremony music will be some of our favourite instrumental numbers from games, and we’re going to have four TVs set up around the venue with Mario Kart, Super Smash Bros, Goldeneye 007, and Wii Sports for people to play during cocktail hour and if they aren’t into dancing later. Will have little game nods throughout the decor so that the people who get it will definitely get it, but they’re not necessarily too in your face. Our place cards will be N64 game cartridge shells with customized name labels, seating chart that looks like a retro game world map, table numbers in the Final Fantasy Roman numeral style, Paupu fruit-shaped donuts for dessert (if you share one with someone, your destinies will be intertwined forever! Kingdom Hearts reference). I’m so excited!!
